description:
Deep Rest Music | Slow Surbahar | 1.5 Hours of Stillness

If your body is exhausted but your mind won't stop scrolling possibilities — start here. 1.5 hours of slow surbahar designed for deep rest and nervous system release.

Some evenings need silence. Some need surbahar. The deepest of the Indian plucked string instruments, surbahar's low resonant tones are designed to tell a stretched-thin nervous system: you can stop now.

🎵 What you'll hear:
- Surbahar — the deep, slow Indian string instrument (think slowed-down sitar)
- Long sustained notes matched to slow breathing rhythm
- A gentle Theta wave layer for nervous system to soften
- Unbroken sound — no abrupt fades, no startling moments

⏱ Chapters
0:00   Settling in
12:00  Body softening
30:00  Nervous system releasing
60:00  Deep rest zone
80:00  Gentle return

🧠 How to use:
Press play. Lights low. Sit or lie down. Don't try to relax — the slow strings do the work. Phone face down. Headphones recommended for the Theta layer.

⏱ Best for:
• End-of-day decompression
• Wired-but-tired evenings
• Pre-sleep wind-down
• Mental exhaustion / burnout recovery
• Long rest sessions

📺 Subscribe to Raga Focus for daily uploads:
- Sitar, Sarangi, Veena, Surbahar, Bansuri, Tanpura and other Indian instruments
- Music for anxiety, overthinking, sleep, stress, emotional release

— Raga Focus

thumbnail_prompt: Pichwai/Kangra miniature painting style, ornate gold-and-cream patterned border with subtle peacock and lotus motifs, aged warm parchment background, late-evening palette (deep amber with single warm oil lamp glow). Central figure: serene woman in deep-burgundy-and-cream sari with gold accents seated cross-legged playing surbahar (recognizable by its large gourd resonator and long fretted neck — like a slower bigger sitar) in a quiet candle-lit room. Soft warm light through a window. A still water bowl or single drooping flower as visual rest-cue. Bold dark-teal serif overlay text reading 'BODY DRAINED?' top-center, traditional Devanagari-influenced serif typography, high contrast for mobile readability. Aged warm cream parchment palette, contemplative restful mood, single composed scene, no clutter.
suno_prompt: Instrumental only, no vocals. Solo surbahar in raga Darbari Kanada, deep evening rest mood, slow contemplative tempo with sustained low resonant notes, no percussion, no tabla, no melodic lead instruments other than surbahar, 432Hz tuning, 65-70 BPM very slow tempo, deep meend slides and gamak ornamentation with long pauses, cinematic meditation production, deeply grounding, suitable for extended looping in post-production, begins immediately with surbahar already playing, no fade-in, no silent intro, full sonic presence from first note. CRITICAL register notes: surbahar bass register PROMINENT — emphasize the lowest two strings, sustained drone-resolving phrases that BREATHE (not busy). Sparse note density. Long silences between phrases. Recent ships AVD slipping suggests audio may be too dense — counteract by deliberately sparse phrasing. deeply settled, like a body finally surrendering to rest

production_spec.loop_seam: 10s in / 30s out, Suno extend 3-4x → loop in post to fill 90 min
production_spec.notes: EMOTIONAL TAG ROTATION: clip 1: 'deeply settled, like a body finally surrendering to rest' · clip 2: 'deeply introspective, like breath held before release' · clip 3: 'gently hopeful, like tension quietly dissolving' · clips 4-7 cycle. Darbari Kanada tonic A or D. CRITICAL: Surbahar is the BIG version of sitar — deeper register, slower attack, more sustain. Suno may default to sitar — explicitly state 'surbahar', 'deep low register', 'slower than sitar', 'sustained long notes'. AVD WILDCARD: recent ships dropped 6-8 AVD points — audio likely too dense or attack too sharp. For this swing, push sparser phrasing in Suno prompt and verify first clip before committing. Mix: Suno -3dB, Binaural -18dB, Tanpura drone layer -24dB. 432Hz canonical for healing-frequency audience. DIRECT REPLICA of Apr 28 hero (19K views/26% AVD, channel's #2 video).
